nodes.statement: G5 leaves the five timeout failures as the only cohort with zero complete paired coverage: every timeout's last durable event is in_flight, 142 eligible timeout steps are unknown, and no post-run step exists, while the non-timeout cohorts are fully covered and have no negative steps. The bounded problem is whether a write-only, hook-local sidecar in a g005-derived child can assign each observed timeout's last durable operation exactly one coarse tool-class enum and in-flight phase, and record a derived elapsed bucket, without persisting raw tool names, arguments, messages, results, task IDs, answers, hints, validators, or traces and without changing agent-visible behavior or scoring.

nodes.counterexample: The timeout may be caused by a harness kill, resource exhaustion, or an uninterruptible call whose pre-exec record is durable but whose operation class is not the operative cause. A timeout can have a non-unknown class and still reflect no agent-addressable mechanism. Conversely, a timeout may leave no durable pre-exec record, making the class unknown rather than localized. The five G5 timeouts may not recur, and a task can have a fully localized in-flight call yet still fail strict evaluation; localization is not progress or correctness.
nodes.falsification_condition: Contradicted if any observed timeout lacks a durable pre-exec record, has more than one conflicting last-event record, has a last durable matched post-exec completion with no later pre-exec so there is no in-flight call, or if the sidecar persists raw tool names, raw arguments, messages, results, task IDs, answers, hints, validator content, traces, digest strings, credentials, or task content, or changes agent-visible input, dispatch, results, or scoring. The class-distribution subclaim is contradicted if every observed timeout is coarse-classified as answer_return or other. Inconclusive, not falsified, if no timeout occurs, if any observed timeout's coarse class is unknown because the tool name is outside the declared mapping or parsing or canonicalization fails, or if non-timeout coverage is below 0.8. A strict-pass difference alone neither supports nor falsifies.
nodes.prediction: In one formal 56-task no-hint run with the fixed 1200 s limit and strict all-56 scoring: (1) if at least one timeout occurs, every observed timeout receives exactly one last-durable-event record with phase=in_flight and a non-unknown coarse tool class; (2) at least one observed timeout is classified as database_query or python_execution; (3) no observed timeout's last durable record is a matched post-exec completion without a later pre-exec record; (4) non-timeout cohorts show no sidecar-induced change in agent-visible input, dispatch, results, or scoring, and their hook records achieve at least 0.8 complete-task coverage as an inertness check; (5) the strict-pass partition is reported descriptively with no predicted increase.
nodes.statement: In the verified g005 child, an additive write-only sidecar at the existing DataAgentWithSelfObservation._handle_tool_call hook will make the timeout in-flight interval locally interpretable: for each observed timeout, the last durable pre-exec record will be the unique unmatched call, and its in-memory coarse class will be one of database_query, python_execution, answer_return, other, or unknown; at least one observed timeout will be classified as database_query or python_execution; and the sidecar will not change agent-visible inputs, dispatch, results, or scoring. This is a localization claim about instrumentation, not a claim about task progress, correctness, or causal gain.

nodes.implementation_scope: One hook-local sidecar in a new child of g005; one durable pre-exec append and one durable post-exec finished append per hook invocation, plus an optional best-effort task-end summary. The fixed mapping must cover the parent's finite tool-name set before launch; any unmapped or unparseable name is unknown, and raw names are discarded. The G5 derived-elapsed computation and validation are reused without changing their epsilon or clock-domain rules. No new tool, task, prompt, policy sentence, timing limit, retry taxonomy, second arm, sham run, probe run, or extra formal evaluation. If the post-exec boundary cannot be observed without reading tool results, messages, or task content, or if the sidecar cannot be proven write-only and inert, do not launch. Tool identity is not compared across live and post-run boundaries; the sidecar records only the coarse enum.
nodes.intervention: Add one additive, write-only sidecar in a g005-derived child alongside the existing G5 provenance sidecar. At the existing DataAgentWithSelfObservation._handle_tool_call hook, before tool dispatch, read tool_name and parsed_tool_args only in memory, map the exact tool name through a fixed predeclared enum to database_query, python_execution, answer_return, other, or unknown, and durably append only anonymous_task_index, hook_local_step_ordinal, event_phase=pre_exec, coarse_tool_class, and a derived elapsed bucket or unknown computed from the existing G5 clock-domain validation. Immediately after the wrapped call returns or raises, in a finally block that re-raises unchanged, durably append event_phase=post_exec_finished, the same ordinal, and a completion_boolean, without reading exception content. At task end, optionally append a summary containing only the same allowed fields and aggregate counts. Do not persist raw tool names, raw arguments, messages, results, task IDs, answers, hints, validator content, traces, digest strings, credentials, or task content. Do not block, retry, mutate arguments, inject messages, feed the agent, change tool dispatch or error handling, alter result storage, or alter scoring. The existing G5 sidecar and all frozen artifacts remain unchanged.

measurement_plan.coarse_tool_class_mapping: In memory only: exact tool_name query_db maps to database_query; execute_python maps to python_execution; return_answer maps to answer_return; any other declared parent tool maps to other; missing, unparseable, or outside the predeclared finite mapping maps to unknown. The mapping is fixed before launch and uniform across tasks; raw names are never persisted.
measurement_plan.cohort_aggregation: Report task and step counts separately for known strict fail, strict pass, strict-verdict unknown, and timeout failure. For each cohort report coverage-positive, coverage-negative, and coverage-unknown tasks; pre-exec and post-exec record counts; timeout positive, negative, and unknown counts; last-event class counts; elapsed-bucket counts; and unmatched pre-exec counts. Never pool cohorts to mask missing coverage. The strict-pass partition and any score difference are descriptive and are never treated as correctness or causal evidence.
measurement_plan.contradicted_conditions: Contradicted if any observed timeout is negative; any non-timeout task shows sidecar-induced agent-visible change; prohibited content is persisted; or the class-distribution subclaim fails because every observed timeout is classified as answer_return or other. An unknown coarse class is not a contradiction by itself.
measurement_plan.coverage_denominator: The overall denominator is the fixed 56 tasks. After the frozen evaluator runs, each cohort denominator is the observed number of tasks in known strict fail, strict pass, strict-verdict unknown, or timeout failure; G5 reference counts 19, 30, 2, and 5 are not reused as denominators. Non-timeout complete-task coverage is the number of coverage-positive tasks divided by the observed cohort denominator. Timeout localization coverage is the number of timeout-positive tasks divided by the observed timeout denominator. Report numerator, denominator, and rate separately.
measurement_plan.coverage_task_negative_rule: For a non-timeout task, coverage-negative if any eligible step has multiple or conflicting records, if the sidecar changes agent-visible input, dispatch, results, or scoring, or if prohibited content is persisted.
measurement_plan.coverage_task_positive_rule: For a non-timeout task, coverage-positive when it has at least one eligible reviewed-hook step and every eligible step has exactly one pre-exec record and one matching post-exec finished record at the same ordinal with the same non-unknown coarse_tool_class; completion_boolean may be true or false.
measurement_plan.coverage_task_unknown_rule: For a non-timeout task, coverage-unknown if it has no eligible hook steps, any eligible step lacks a pre-exec or matching post-exec finished record, or its coarse class is unknown.
measurement_plan.coverage_threshold: A 0.8 complete-task coverage threshold applies only to non-timeout cohorts for the sidecar-coverage and inertness report; below 0.8 withholds cohort coverage support and is an Evidence result, not a launch veto. No coverage threshold is applied to timeout-localization support: the rule is all observed timeouts positive. With zero observed timeouts, the timeout component is untested.
measurement_plan.elapsed_bucket_rule: Reuse the G5 validated derived elapsed value and assign fixed buckets 0-120 s, greater than 120 through 600 s, greater than 600 through 1200 s, or unknown. If G5 clock-domain validation fails or elapsed is nonmonotone, assign unknown; never persist raw deadline, spawn-remaining, monotonic, or baseline values.
measurement_plan.inconclusive_conditions: Timeout-class localization is inconclusive if no timeout occurs, any observed timeout is unknown, or required fields are missing. Non-timeout coverage and inertness are inconclusive for a cohort with complete-task coverage below 0.8 or no eligible steps. A strict-pass difference alone is inconclusive.
measurement_plan.no_answer_no_hint_boundary: The sidecar may read only the declared source fields. It may read tool_name and parsed_tool_args in memory solely to compute the coarse tool class and any existing G5 canonical category, and must immediately discard them; it must not persist or expose raw tool names, raw argument payloads, benchmark answers, hints, validators, expected outputs, task IDs, raw traces, messages, tool results, credentials, network content, digest strings, or task content. It may read the hook-local monotonic clock, DAB_TASK_DEADLINE_MONOTONIC, DAB_TASK_SPAWN_REMAINING_SEC, and the fixed 1200 s protocol limit solely to derive a bounded elapsed bucket or unknown, and must not persist raw clock values. Cohort labels and strict verdicts are joined only after the run and are never read by the agent or sidecar during execution. All rules are uniform algorithms over normal task-visible inputs; no task IDs or post-run strict verdicts define agent behavior. The sidecar never feeds the agent or alters control or scoring.
measurement_plan.run_before: All rules, enums, tool-class mapping, elapsed buckets, coverage denominator, coverage threshold, and unknown fallbacks are fixed before child implementation or formal execution; no post-run strict verdict, task ID, answer, hint, or validator defines a rule.
measurement_plan.runtime_hook: DataAgentWithSelfObservation._handle_tool_call in the g005 code parent: pre-exec observation before tool dispatch, post-exec finished observation in a finally block immediately after the wrapped call returns or raises, and an optional best-effort task-end summary. Timeout classification uses the last durable pre-exec or post-exec finished event and does not require the summary. The sidecar is write-only and is never read by the agent.
measurement_plan.supported_conditions: Timeout-class localization is supported if at least one timeout is observed and every observed timeout is positive under the timeout rule. The class-distribution subclaim is supported only if at least one observed timeout is classified as database_query or python_execution. Non-timeout sidecar coverage and inertness are supported for a cohort if complete-task coverage is at least 0.8 and no coverage-negative or behavior-changing record is observed. The strict-pass partition is not part of support.
measurement_plan.timeout_task_negative_rule: An observed timeout task is negative if its last durable event is a post-exec finished record with no later pre-exec, if more than one unmatched pre-exec record exists, if last-event pairing is conflicting, if prohibited content is persisted, or if the sidecar changes agent-visible input, dispatch, results, or scoring. A timeout with an unknown coarse class is not negative merely for being unknown.
measurement_plan.timeout_task_positive_rule: An observed timeout task is positive only when the frozen evaluator labels it timeout_failure, the sidecar has exactly one durable pre-exec record with no later pre-exec and no matching post-exec finished record at the same ordinal, the last durable event has event_phase=pre_exec and terminal_status=in_flight, and its coarse_tool_class is non-unknown. A task-end summary is not required.
measurement_plan.timeout_task_unknown_rule: An observed timeout task is unknown if it has no durable pre-exec or post-exec finished record, its coarse_tool_class is unknown, its last-event pairing is ambiguous, or required fields are missing. A unique unmatched pre-exec record is the in-flight positive condition, not an unknown condition.
measurement_plan.unit: per_task for timeout localization and coverage; per_step for pre-exec and post-exec record matching

limits: A coarse in-flight class localizes an operation, not the cause of timeout or task correctness.
Timeouts are failures in the fixed 56 denominator; unavailable records remain unknown.
Three completed strict verdicts remain unknown and are not reclassified.
This is one unpaired run; score differences from earlier generations are descriptive only.
nodes.statement: G6 coarse tool-class and elapsed-bucket timeout localization on the frozen no-hint 56.
